questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) The following are components of an Industrial system;
Weaving, Cloth, power, Carpets, Labour, bleaching land, bags, buildings, dying.
(i) Arrange the components under; Inputs, Process and outputs (Tabulate your answer)
(ii) Outline THREE reasons why the level of industrialization in developing countries is low.

(5 + 3 = 8marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Arranging the components of the industrial system (5 marks).** An industrial system has **inputs** (what is put in: raw materials, power, labour, capital, land, buildings), a **process** (what is done to the inputs in the factory) and **outputs** (the goods that come out). The ten components of a textile factory are classified as follows (the list in the paper reads "bleaching land", which is two items, **bleaching** and **land**).

| Inputs | Process | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| **Power** | **Weaving** | **Cloth** |
| **Labour** | **Bleaching** | **Carpets** |
| **Land** | **Dyeing** (printed "dying") | **Bags** |
| **Buildings** | | |

Half a mark for each correctly placed component (ten components, 5 marks); a correct table with the three headings is required.

**(ii) Three reasons why the level of industrialisation in developing countries is low (3 marks, 1 mark each).**

1. **Shortage of capital.** Industries need a lot of money to build factories and buy machines, but governments and individuals in developing countries have little money to invest and borrowing is costly.
2. **Low level of technology and a lack of skilled labour and of managers.** Many workers are not trained, technical education is limited and the machines and know-how have to be imported.
3. **Small local markets.** Most people have a low income and a low purchasing power, so there are few customers; goods also face competition from cheaper imports.
4. **Poor infrastructure.** Roads, railways, electricity and water supply are often poor or expensive, which raises the cost of production.
5. **Other reasons:** political instability and corruption, dependence on the export of raw materials (agriculture and mining) rather than their processing, and the effects of the colonial economic system.

(Any three are enough.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Suggest THREE ways in which the tourism sector can be made more attractive.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three ways (2 marks each: the suggestion and a short explanation).

1. **Improve the infrastructure.** Build and maintain **roads, airports, railways, electricity and water supply**, and build more hotels, restaurants and rest houses of good quality, so that tourists can reach the sites and stay comfortably.
2. **Develop, protect and promote the tourist sites.** Maintain the national parks, museums, beaches, waterfalls and cultural sites (for example the palaces and museums of the chiefdoms), create new attractions and festivals, and **advertise** them widely (television, internet, tourism fairs, embassies abroad), so that more visitors know the country.
3. **Guarantee security and simplify the entry procedures.** Maintain peace and the safety of visitors, fight against corruption and harassment, make the **visa and customs procedures simpler** and the **prices reasonable**.
4. **Train the staff.** Train tour guides and hotel workers in hospitality and in foreign languages, so that tourists receive a good welcome.

(Any three are enough.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Outline FOUR advantages of HEP over other sources of energy.
(ii) State TWO renewable sources of energy.

(2 + 4 = 6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Four advantages of hydroelectric power (HEP) over other sources of energy (4 marks, 1 mark each).**

1. **It is renewable.** The water is not used up: it returns to the rivers through the hydrological cycle, while coal, oil and gas are **exhaustible**.
2. **It is clean.** HEP stations do not burn fuel, so they give off **no smoke or greenhouse gases** and cause much less air pollution than thermal stations.
3. **It is cheap to run and the stations last long.** After the high cost of construction, the **running costs are low** (no fuel to buy or to transport) and the dams and turbines work for many decades.
4. **It is multi-purpose.** The reservoir behind the dam is also used for **irrigation, water supply, flood control, fishing, navigation and tourism**.
5. HEP can be **started or stopped quickly** to follow the demand for electricity, and it reduces the **need to import fuel**. In Cameroon, the Edea and Song Loulou stations on the River Sanaga and the Lagdo station on the River Benue are examples.

(Any four are enough.)

**(ii) Two renewable sources of energy (2 marks, 1 mark each).** **Solar energy** and **wind energy**. (Also accepted: biomass or biogas, geothermal energy, tidal and wave energy, and hydroelectric power.)
